tagline: Volcanic-soil durian, Khmer temples, and the Khao Phra Wihan border trail in the deep south of Isan
introHtml: Sisaket is a southern Isan province that lately got on the map for its volcanic-soil durian, grown on volcanic earth around Kantharalak and prized for a flavor all its own. When durian season hits, people drive straight to the orchards to eat it on the spot. The province also has old Khmer temples scattered across several districts, the Pha Mo I Daeng cliff and the trail up to Khao Phra Wihan along the border, and a mix of ethnic communities — Lao, Khmer, Suay, and Yoe — all living side by side. It's a place to take slowly, where you get nature, good food, and traces of history all at once.
bestTime: November–February for cool, easy travel weather; if you're here for the volcanic-soil durian, come in June–July.

highlights.name: Kantharalak volcanic-soil durian
highlights.blurb: The specialty that put Sisaket on the map. Grown on volcanic soil around Kantharalak and Khun Han, the flesh is dry, crisp outside and soft inside, and not too sweet. In season people go eat it right at the orchards.

highlights.name: Pha Mo I Daeng
highlights.blurb: A rock cliff on the Thai–Cambodian border in Kantharalak district, looking out over Cambodian land. Ancient bas-relief carvings line the cliff face — a viewpoint and the route toward Khao Phra Wihan.

highlights.name: Prasat Sa Kamphaeng Yai
highlights.blurb: The most complete Khmer temple in Sisaket, in Uthumphon Phisai district, with brick prangs and beautifully carved lintels.

highlights.name: Wat Lan Khuat
highlights.blurb: The 'Million Bottle Temple' (Wat Pa Maha Chedi Kaeo) in Khun Han district, decorated throughout with over a million old glass bottles. A popular photo stop.

highlights.name: Wat Phra That Rueang Rong
highlights.blurb: A temple near the city with a chedi built in the blended architecture of Sisaket's four peoples — Lao, Khmer, Suay, and Yoe — reflecting the mix of communities here.

highlights.name: Sisaket shallots and garlic
highlights.blurb: A long-standing local product. The shallots are tight-cloved and pungent, grown widely enough to be a cash crop — easy to grab as a gift to take home.

foodScene.name: Southern Isan food
foodScene.note: Som tam, larb, koi, grilled chicken — bold flavors you can find all over town, with a Khmer touch at some places near the border.

foodScene.name: Volcanic-soil durian
foodScene.note: The star of the province in durian season — dry flesh, crisp outside and soft inside, not too sweet. During fruit season you can taste it at the orchards around Kantharalak and Khun Han.

foodScene.name: Shallots and garlic
foodScene.note: A signature local crop. The shallots are tight-cloved and pungent and grown widely — buy them as a gift, or fry them into crispy shallots.

foodScene.name: Khanom chin Pradok
foodScene.note: Rice noodles in a rich Isan-style curry broth, eaten with a big pile of fresh vegetables. A popular breakfast for locals.

foodScene.name: Pla som and homemade naem
foodScene.note: Local fermented preserves with a mellow sour tang — fried up with hot steamed rice, or bought to take along.

foodScene.name: Thung Kula jasmine rice
foodScene.note: Jasmine rice from the Thung Kula area in the province. It cooks up fragrant and soft — quality rice people buy to bring home.

foodScene.name: Cafes and evening markets in town
foodScene.note: The town center has small cafes and an evening market that gathers street food and snacks for grazing after dark.

attractions.name: Pha Mo I Daeng
attractions.blurb: A border cliff in Kantharalak district — a viewpoint over Cambodian land, with ancient bas-relief carvings on the rock face.

attractions.name: Khao Phra Wihan National Park
attractions.blurb: A border park with waterfalls, a twin stupa, and hiking trails, serving as the link to the Khao Phra Wihan temple on the Thai side.

attractions.name: Prasat Sa Kamphaeng Yai
attractions.blurb: The most complete Khmer temple in the province, with several brick prangs and beautifully carved lintels.

attractions.name: Prasat Prasat (Ban Prasat)
attractions.blurb: A small sandstone Khmer temple in Huai Thap Than district, standing out in the middle of the community — close-up views of Khmer artistry.

attractions.name: Wat Lan Khuat
attractions.blurb: The 'Million Bottle Temple' (Wat Pa Maha Chedi Kaeo) in Khun Han district, decorated with over a million old glass bottles. A popular photo stop.

attractions.name: Wat Phra That Rueang Rong
attractions.blurb: A temple near the city with a chedi in the blended architecture of four peoples, reflecting the mix of communities here.

attractions.name: Volcanic-soil durian orchards
attractions.blurb: Orchards around Kantharalak and Khun Han that open for on-the-spot tasting in fruit season — see the durian trees growing on real volcanic soil.

attractions.name: Huai Nam Kham island park
attractions.blurb: A public park in the center of Sisaket with a mid-water island and the city pillar shrine — a spot where locals relax and exercise.
